I’ve just examined the plugin worker manager code to understand how workers are started and reused. The relevant snippet shows that when a plugin is requested, the manager checks `workers.get(pluginId)` and, if a worker already exists and isn’t stopped, it reuses it rather than spawning a new one. This means that after I edited the Groq adapter plugin files (execute.js and paperclip-tools.js), the changes will only take effect when the corresponding plugin worker process is restarted. 

I need to verify whether the Groq plugin worker is currently running, and if so, whether it’s the old version that still has the duplicate‑execution bug. If the worker is already running, I’ll have to restart it (or the whole server) to load the updated code. Conversely, if there is no worker process, I can be confident that the next request will spawn a fresh worker with the new code.

To check this, I should look for any Node processes that correspond to the Groq adapter plugin or the generic plugin worker. A simple `ps aux` filtered for “groq”, “plugin‑worker”, or “adapter‑plugin” will list any such processes. I’ll also exclude the grep command itself with `grep -v grep`. This will give me a clear view of whether the worker is alive and needs a restart.
